messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: elevated queue length on inference-prod across us-west-2 GPUs, latency P95 > 4s, error rate spiking for embedding calls. Auto-page sent to oncall.
ana: looking now, seeing large tail on embedding endpoints, traffic surge from a single customer namespace (tenant-batch-42).
mike: confirmed. max_in_flight metrics climbed from 180 -> 260 and request_timeouts rising.
runtime-oncall: can we shed long-running embeddings first? prefer targeted mitigations before global changes.
jess: customer is running a big embedding job; it's filling KV cache and blocking short chat requests. cs-rep: pinged customer (acct: batch-inc) to pause, waiting on response.
ana: plan proposal: 1) apply tenant-level rate cap 60rps for tenant-batch-42 2) bump global per-request timeout 60->30s for embeddings 3) lower max_in_flight on embedding pool from 220 -> 120 4) enable shedding for requests >30s.
mike: agree with priority ordering. we should also disable experimental reranker on embeddings to reduce SU.
runtime-oncall: ready to apply changes. pushing config to live canary (10% traffic) first. snippet:```bash
# runtime config
pools.embedding.max_in_flight=120
routes./v1/embeddings.timeout_sec=30
quotas.tenant-batch-42.rate_limit_rps=60
features.experimental_reranker=false
shedding.threshold_ms=30000
```
ana: applying canary now. alerting monitoring to watch p95/p99 and queue length.
jess: cs-rep reports customer acknowledged and will throttle on their side if we request.
mike: rollback plan: if p99 latency does not drop within 3m or errors increase, revert max_in_flight and timeout immediately and escalate to infra.
runtime-oncall: canary applied at 12:03 UTC. initial telemetry: queue length down 35%, p95 embeddings down to 1.6s, but chat tail unchanged yet.
ana: pushing full rollout to embedding pool now. also adding an aggressive token-level circuit breaker for embedding size > 512 to shed heavy requests.
mike: noted — will inform product and ops. tagging for postmortem: ana + mike + runtime-oncall + jess.
cs-rep: Customer reported degraded throughput but accepted temporary rate cap. no SLA hits yet; monitoring for errors.
runtime-oncall: full rollout complete at 12:07 UTC. observed sustained p95 improvement and error rate returning to normal.
ana: closing mitigation loop. follow-ups: 1) schedule a quota policy to prevent single-tenant saturation 2) add anomaly detection on KV-cache fill rate 3) postmortem to capture lessons.
mike: thanks team. leaving handoff notes for next oncall in #eng-oncall-shifts. :thumbsup:
